info.title: Conspect Control API
info.description: REST + WebSocket + SSE management API for the Conspect engine.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/account/audit` — the append-only account audit log, paginated
(role: read).
get.description:
Returns `{entries, next_cursor}`: entries oldest-first within the page,
resumable via `?cursor=next_cursor`, optionally `?filter=<kind>`. There is no
mutating verb on this resource — the log is append-only by construction.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Resume strictly after this `seq` cursor (from a previous `next_cursor`).
Absent fetches from the beginning of the log.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Restrict the listing to a single action kind (`kebab-case` slug).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
The maximum number of entries to return (clamped to
[`MAX_AUDIT_PAGE_LIMIT`]; defaults to [`DEFAULT_AUDIT_PAGE_LIMIT`]).

200.description: A page of account-audit entries (oldest-first) + the resume cursor.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

get.description:
Returns the actions awaiting local execution or cancellation, oldest-first.
An action that has executed or been cancelled drops out of this list.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/actions/{id}/cancel` — cancel a pending action locally (role:
write).
post.description:
**Local always wins:** a pending action the operator cancels here is
cancelled, and any later (portal-fed) execution attempt is refused. An action
that has **already executed** answers `410 Gone` `already_executed` — the
truthful "too late", never a fake success. An unknown id is `404`. The cancel
is recorded in the append-only account audit store.

200.description: The action was pending and is now cancelled (local wins).

410.description: The action has already executed — too late to cancel.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Keep only alarms at or above this X.733 severity (e.g. `major`).

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Keep only active (`true`) or only cleared/historical (`false`) alarms.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Keep only alarms whose scope kind matches (e.g. `tile`, `probe`).

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/alarms/{id}/ack` — acknowledge an alarm (role: write; If-Match).

get.description:
**404-free**: an unconfigured deployment answers `200` with
`configured: false`, `routing: null`, and `selectable_tracks: ["prog"]`
(the program bus is always selectable). The response `ETag` is the document
version a later `PUT` must present as `If-Match`.

200.description: The audio-routing document (404-free: `configured: false` + a null document when none is set; ETag in the response header).

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

put.summary:
`PUT /api/v1/audio-routing` — replace the singleton document (role: write;
`If-Match` required → `428`/`412`).

200.description: The replaced document (new ETag in the response header; X-Multiview-Apply: live when the running program bus applied it, restart when it needs a restart, e.g. a changed sample rate).

422.description: The body is not a valid audio-routing document (detail names the field path or the violated routing invariant; references to undeclared sources are checked at config export, not here).

get.description: An optional `?object_id=` filters to a single object's history.

parameters.name: object_id
parameters.description: Restrict the listing to a single object id.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/cast/sessions` — list the live ephemeral sessions (role: read).

200.description: All live ephemeral sessions, id-sorted, each with its live lifecycle state.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/cast/sessions` — start an ad-hoc cast session (role: write).
post.description:
Resolves the rendition, spawns the supervised session actor through the
shared poller registry, and records the ephemeral session. The actor
CONNECTs → `LAUNCH`es the Default Media Receiver (`CC1AD845`) → `LOAD`s the
device-reachable HLS URL, then supervises the session (ADR-M011).

201.description: The started ephemeral session (runtime-only; never exported).

403.description: Not authorized to start a session.

409.description: No castable rendition (control.cast_media_base unset / no HLS output) or no live cast driver in this build.

422.description: The address is not a valid host[:port], or the named output is not a served HLS rendition.

200.description: The session, with its live lifecycle state.

403.description: Not authorized to read this session.

404.description: No live session with that id.

delete.description:
Dispatches the voluntary [`PollerControl::StopCast`] teardown (the actor
`STOP`s the receiver app — what actually clears the TV — then exits), joins
it gracefully (abort after the grace window), drops the runtime
status/record, and **clears the registry tombstone**: session ids are
UUID-fresh and never reused, so clearing after the deterministic stop keeps
the tombstone set bounded under churning sessions.

204.description: The session was stopped and forgotten.

403.description: Not authorized to stop this session.

404.description: No live session with that id.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/cast/sessions/{id}/save` — promote an ephemeral session to a
normal `Device{driver: cast}` registry entry (role: write; `201`).
post.description:
The promoted device carries the session's address and rendition assignment
and **does** export (desired state). One actor remains, keyed by the device
id: the ephemeral actor is stopped (a plain abort — **no** receiver `STOP`,
so the TV keeps playing across the promotion) and the device's supervised
actor takes over through the same registry.

201.description: The promoted device (ETag in the response header).

404.description: No live session with that id.

409.description: A device with that id already exists.

422.description: The promoted device document does not validate.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/cast/sessions/{id}/volume` — set the receiver volume
(role: write; `202` + operation id).
post.description:
Dispatches a receiver-namespace `SET_VOLUME` to the running session actor
— non-blocking `try_send`, never awaited (invariant #10).

202.description: Volume change accepted; applied by the session actor.

403.description: Not authorized to control this session.

404.description: No live session with that id.

422.description: level_percent is out of range (0–100).

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/catalogues/iptv-org/import` — offline bundle import (administer).

requestBody.description: A JSON object keyed by upstream file name (`streams`, `channels`, `feeds`, `logos`, `cities`, `countries`, `subdivisions`, `regions`, `blocklist`, `categories`, `languages`), optionally gzip'd. Replaces the named files; the rest stay as persisted.

422.description: Bundle is malformed.

200.description: `{schema, generated_at, categories[], languages[], streams[]}`; gzip when accepted; identical for every caller (`already_added` is computed by the web).

503.description: No snapshot yet; refresh or import first.

200.description: `{links: [{source_id, status, checked_at, upstream, replaced_by, alternatives}]}` — status, upstream target and ranked alternatives (with cached probe verdict), only for sources the caller may see.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Logo key `l:<hex>` from an index row.

200.description: The logo image (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/SVG), size-capped, cached on disk for 30 days. `Cache-Control: private, max-age=2592000, immutable` and a strong `ETag`.

204.description: No logo: unknown key, upstream missing/failing, oversized or not an image (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`), or the upstream fetch queue was busy (`Cache-Control: no-store`; retry later). Never an error status.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/catalogues/iptv-org/probes` — start a probe job (operate).

202.description: The probe job `{id, state: queued|running|done|failed, results[], error}`; poll `GET probes/{id}`. A 15-minute cache hit completes immediately.

403.description: Requires operate (write), or a `source_ids` entry the caller may not use.

422.description: `keys` + `source_ids` must hold 1..=50 entries.

429.description: Per-principal rate (60/min) or the global queue (64) is exhausted.

503.description: No probe service on this node.

200.description: The probe job and its finished results (verdict, facts, events).

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/catalogues/iptv-org/refresh` — sync now (administer).

200.description: `{outcome: unchanged|updated, changed[]}`; a failed sync keeps the previous snapshot.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/catalogues/iptv-org/sources` — bulk-create sources (write).

201.description: Every source was created; per-item results in request order.

207.description: A durable write failed part-way: earlier items are created, the failed item and the rest are reported.

403.description: Requires write, or an id is outside the caller's scope.

422.description: More than 200 sources in one bulk add; or more than 8 with an entry that leaves its `activation` implicit; or an entry is invalid or duplicated. Nothing was created.

200.description: Sync state, counts, ETags, last error and the caller-scoped link-status tally.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: audit, permissions, scoped-token, relays, provision, import, update, teardown, observe, rotate, rotation-installed, revoke, revoke-token, detach, set-mode, reconcile, recover, adopt-recovery, acknowledge-recovery, capabilities

503.description: Management unavailable

post.description:
The stored layout body is resolved from the layouts repository and solved
**here, at request time** (off the engine hot path): an unknown id, a body
that does not parse as a `{canvas, layout, cells}` document, one that does
not solve (bad grid / geometry), a pinned-canvas mismatch (a Class-2
change — ADR-R004), or an unknown running canvas (no seeded snapshot — the
gate fails closed) is an honest `422` **before** any `202`. On `202` the
command carries the solved layout, so the engine's frame-boundary drain
only swaps (O(cells), no I/O — invariants #1/#10); the `202` body's
`applied_live`/`carried_only` arrays state which per-cell property classes
genuinely apply on screen. Idempotency reserves **before** resolution: a
replayed `Idempotency-Key` returns the original operation id (kind
`replay`, undecorated) without re-resolving, and a refused resolve
releases the key. The submit mirrors [`cmd_swap`] (shed-on-full) and never
blocks the engine (invariant #10); the outcome rides the realtime stream
as a `job.progress` event (ADR-W008).

202.description: Apply-layout accepted: the stored layout was resolved + solved and will swap in at the next frame boundary; `applied_live`/`carried_only` state the property classes. Outcome on the realtime stream (`job.progress`).

403.description: Not authorized to apply a layout.

422.description: The layout id does not exist, its stored body does not parse/solve, its canvas differs from the running session's pinned canvas (Class-2), the running canvas is unknown (no seeded snapshot — the gate fails closed), or a switcher M/E is declared and the layout is not one full-canvas cell bound to its program source (type `/problems/layout-not-admissible-with-switcher`; nothing is applied or persisted).

503.description: Engine command bus at capacity; shed.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/config/boot-model` — the Boot/Loaded/Running model status
(ADR-W024 §7; role: read).
get.description:
Reports whether this run carries a boot model, the boot path and start
policy, whether the run resumed (+ the fallback reason), the per-section
divergence of Running from the Loaded snapshot and from the current boot
file, and the last `active.toml` write time.

200.description: The Boot/Loaded/Running model status with per-section divergence.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

422.description: The live stores do not compose into a valid Running document.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/config/export` — render the live resource stores as a complete
`multiview.toml` document (ADR-W015).
get.description:
Composes the working layout (the id-sorted first layout whose body carries a
`canvas`) with every stored source/output/overlay/probe into a
[`multiview_config::MultiviewConfig`], validates the whole document, and
returns it as TOML. This closes the management loop honestly today: edit in
the UI → export → persist as the config file → the next start applies it.

**Secrets are redacted.** The export is outward-facing, so every inline
cleartext secret (WebRTC ICE `password`/`static_auth_secret`, WHIP/WHEP/
`whip_push` bearer `token`s, and any other secret-class field — see
[`crate::support_bundle::redact_config_for_export`]) is replaced with the
`<redacted>` placeholder. A `secret_ref` pointer (`op://…`) is preserved (it is
not a secret). The placeholder keeps the document re-importable, but it is a
**clearly-marked placeholder**: the operator restores the real credential (or
confirms the `secret_ref`) before the exported file is used to run — the
placeholder never authenticates.

422.description: The stores do not compose into a valid configuration (detail names the violation).

post.description:
Compose → validate → render TOML → announce the write through the
installed ADR-W020 watcher's `expect_write` suppression seam (this is
the seam's designed caller — the watcher adopts the write as its new
baseline without re-applying) → atomic write to the boot path → a
config-versioning commit (target `boot`) → audit. With no watcher
installed there is nothing to suppress and the step is skipped.

200.description: The Running document was written to the boot file and committed as a `boot` config revision.

409.description: This run has no boot model (no config file); there is no boot file to promote to.

422.description: The live stores do not compose into a valid Running document.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/config/revert-to-start` — Running := Loaded, live
(ADR-W024 §5; role: write; `Idempotency-Key`; audited).
post.description:
Composes the current Running document, diffs it against the immutable
Loaded snapshot, and applies the diff through the ONE ADR-W020
diff→apply machinery ([`crate::config_watch::apply_document_diff`]) under
the requesting principal: synthetic source changes ride
`UpsertSource`/`RemoveSource` on the bounded bus, layout/cells ride the
shared resolve+solve+Class-1 gate, stores resync to the Loaded values, and
restart-only sections are reported honestly. The ADR-W020 watcher's file
baseline is deliberately untouched (it tracks the last applied FILE
content). An empty diff applies nothing and reports `reverted: false`.

This is a distinct operator capability from the config-versioning
`POST /config/{target}/rollback` (which restores a prior committed
revision of one tracked document): revert-to-start returns the whole
Running state to the deliberate cold-start baseline, live (ADR-W024 §1).

202.description: The revert was applied (or was an honest no-op) with a per-section summary.

409.description: This run has no boot model (no config file); there is no start state to revert to.

422.description: The live stores do not compose into a valid Running document.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/config/watch-status` — the config-file watch status
(ADR-W020; role: read).
get.description:
Reports whether this process watches its boot config file for external
edits, the watched path, the last applied/rejected loads, and the
restart-pending section names. A store-only deployment (no watcher)
honestly reports `active: false`.

200.description: The config-file watch status: active flag, watched path, last applied/rejected loads, restart-pending sections.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.
Authenticated but not authorized to read.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/devices/{id}` — fetch one device (role: read; per-object authz).

200.description: The device (ETag in the response header).

403.description: Not authorized to read this device.

200.description: The replaced device (new ETag in the response header).

422.description: The body is not a valid device document (detail names the field path).

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}` — adopt/create a device (role: write).
post.description:
Validates the body against `multiview_config::Device` (`422` on an invalid
document), seeds the runtime status registry in `ADOPTING` so
`GET /devices/{id}/status` answers immediately, and **starts the device's
supervised driver poller** (DEV-A4) — which performs the first probe and
drives the device to `ONLINE`/`AUTH_FAILED`/`UNREACHABLE`. The poller is a
no-op for devices the factory does not manage (the default build / a
non-`zowietek` driver).

201.description: The adopted device (ETag in the response header; X-Multiview-Apply declares how it takes effect).

422.description: The body is not a valid device document (detail names the field path).

delete.description:
Refused `409 /problems/conflict` while any Source or Output still references
this device via `device_ref` (ADR-M009): the problem detail names the
blocking resource so the operator knows what to unbind. The delete is never
partially applied — a refused delete leaves the device intact.

409.description: A Source/Output still references this device via device_ref.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/identify` — flash the device's identify indicator
(role: write; fire-and-forget `204`).

get.description:
Returns the device's running driver's enumerated targets (DEV-A4: a
decoder-mode `zowietek` box's decode-table slots). Honestly empty until a
driver has enumerated — and on a build/device with no live driver — never
fabricated live telemetry.

200.description: The declared output targets (empty until a driver enumerates).

403.description: Not authorized to read this device.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/probe` — re-probe the device now (role: write).
post.description:
A synchronous management verb (ADR-W017): it confirms the device exists and
acknowledges the probe request (`200`). The device's supervised driver poller
(DEV-A4) is already probing on its own ≤1 Hz cadence and re-probing on
reconnect, so the latest status is read via `GET /devices/{id}/status`; this
verb is the operator's explicit "I looked" acknowledgement.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/reboot` — reboot the device (role: write; `202`).
post.description:
A long-running management verb (ADR-W017): the operation id is minted and
`202`'d; the outcome arrives on the realtime stream once the driver lands.

202.description: Reboot accepted; outcome on the realtime stream.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/set-mode` — converge the device to a mode
(role: write; `202` + operation id + declared DEV-class impact).
post.description:
The device-side impact is **declared in the body before apply** (ADR-M009):
the device restarts its pipeline; bound sources ride the tile ladder to
`NO_SIGNAL` during the switch; no Conspect output is interrupted. The route
mints the operation id, `202`s, and **dispatches** the convergence to the
device's running driver poller (DEV-A4), which records the requested mode as
its desired mode, runs `plan_mode_convergence` → `converge_mode`
(close-before-open), and publishes the `device.mode` outcome on the realtime
stream; a failed apply is re-converged on the poller's next adopt/reconnect
pass. When no live poller is running (the default build / a device with no
spawned driver), the `202` still declares the impact but nothing applies the
change: the device's configured `desired_mode` is what a later-spawned
poller converges onto when its adopt/reconnect reaches `ONLINE`.

202.description: Mode change accepted (impact declared); outcome on the realtime stream.

403.description: Not authorized to change the mode.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/set-mode/plan` — classify a `set-mode` without
applying it (role: read; zero wire calls). A Class-2 plan must be echoed as
`ack_impact` on the apply.

200.description: The impact the apply would incur; nothing was dispatched.

get.description:
Returns the device's running driver's enumerated candidates (DEV-A4: a
`zowietek` device's served RTSP mounts). Honestly empty until a driver has
enumerated — and on a build/device with no live driver — never fabricated
live telemetry.

200.description: The declared source candidates (empty until a driver enumerates).

403.description: Not authorized to read this device.

get.description:
Reads the latest-wins [`DeviceStatusRegistry`](crate::devices::DeviceStatusRegistry)
(never persisted/exported). A freshly-adopted device with no driver probe yet
sits in `ADOPTING`. `404` when the device is not adopted.

200.description: The device's latest-wins runtime status (never persisted).

403.description: Not authorized to read this device.

404.description: No device with that id is adopted.

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/test-pattern` — display a test pattern on the
device (role: write; fire-and-forget `204`).

`POST /api/v1/diagnostics/snapshot` — assemble the §4.2 one-button support
bundle (role: write).
post.description:
Returns `202 {snapshot_id}`; the assembled bundle is then readable at
`GET /api/v1/diagnostics/{id}`. The bundle is logs + engine state (the local
retention buffer), **never** media (ADR-0053, brief §8). Assembly is
synchronous (the buffer is in-memory) but the contract is `202 + id` so a
future asynchronous/large-bundle composer is a non-breaking change. A
`ContextPackExport`-adjacent action is **not** recorded here: the bundle stays
on the machine (no egress) until an explicit operator-approved data request,
which is the audited egress gate, not this assemble step.

202.description: Snapshot assembled; read it back by id.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to write.

get.description: `200` with the bundle when the id is known; `404` (RFC 9457 problem) when not.

403.description: Authenticated but not authorized to read.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/discovery/devices` — the current untrusted inventory snapshot
(role: read).
get.description:
Returns the discovered services found by the most recent scans, AAAA-first
with IPv4 labelled legacy, stale (TTL-expired) rows purged on read. These are
**hints**, not devices: adopting one is the separate `POST /devices/{id}`
confirm-adopt referencing a discovered address (ADR-0041).

200.description: The untrusted discovery inventory (hints requiring explicit confirm-adopt; never devices).

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/discovery/devices/scan` — kick a time-bounded mDNS browse
(role: write; `202` + operation id).
post.description:
The browse runs on a bounded control-plane task: it asks the injected browser
for services within a time budget, classifies each into the **untrusted
inventory** (AAAA-first, TTL-stamped), and publishes a `device.discovered`
event per service, correlated to this operation id via the envelope `corr`
(ADR-RT007). It never creates a device (ADR-0041).

Scans are **single-flight** (one in-flight browse — concurrent `mdns-sd`
browses corrupt each other's listeners/queriers, and one browse at a time is
the ADR-M008 rate limit): a request that arrives while a scan runs
**attaches** to it and is answered with the *running* scan's operation id.
A retried `Idempotency-Key` returns the original operation id without
re-executing the browse (the canonical replay semantics).

202.description: Scan accepted (or attached to the single-flight running scan, or replayed by Idempotency-Key — the operation id names the scan that actually runs); discovered rows stream as device.discovered events correlated via corr and land in the untrusted inventory.

200.description: Streamed JSONL of every source (unscoped administrators only).

post.summary:
`POST /api/v1/health/{code}/ack` — acknowledge the persisted
`accepted-state-rejected` warning (role: write, unscoped; #324).
post.description:
Removes the start-up fallback marker (on the blocking pool, under the
config-mutation lock — file I/O never runs on a runtime worker, and never on
the engine), then publishes `health.warning.cleared` through the
drop-oldest lane (inv #10) and waits briefly for the warning ingest to apply
it. Acknowledging silences the CURRENT alarm only: a later start that still
cannot use the saved configuration raises it again. The saved configuration
is not touched. An unreadable or unparsable marker still counts as pending
and is removed.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Warning code to acknowledge; only `accepted-state-rejected` is acknowledgeable.

204.description: Acknowledged: the persisted marker is removed and the warning cleared.

403.description: Not authorized to acknowledge (read-only role, or a scoped key: this is a whole-system action).

404.description: Not an acknowledgeable code, no config-file run, or nothing pending.

`POST /api/v1/inputs/{id}/events/test` — inject a clearly-labelled synthetic

machine-UI write always advances the timestamp, so it always applies; the LWW

**never** a URL query (that is the SEC-01 leak this replaces). The ticket
carries the caller's full [`Principal`] (role + every scope axis) and its

bearer therefore never appears in a WS/SSE URL.

AccountAuditEntry.description:
One immutable account-audit entry: who did what, and when.

The four spec fields (brief §11: `{at, actor, kind, detail}`) plus a
monotonic `seq` cursor the store assigns on append so pagination is stable
and resumable even when two entries share an `at` timestamp.

actor.description:
The authenticated principal that performed the action (its key id), or a
well-known system actor for machine-originated events — the **actor**.

at_nanos.description:
The media-timeline timestamp (nanoseconds) the action was recorded — the
**when** (`at`).

detail.description:
An optional structured detail (e.g. the lease serial, the salvo name, the
action id). Never contains secrets or raw identifiers (brief §8).

kind.description: The kind of account action — the **kind**.

seq.description:
The monotonic sequence number the store assigned on append — the stable
pagination cursor. Strictly increasing; never reused.

The kind of account-side action an [`AccountAuditEntry`] records.

the brief §10. Serialised `kebab-case` so the slug is stable across the
machine and the portal. `#[non_exhaustive]` so a future account action adds a
variant without breaking the wire contract.

this page reached the end of the log. Opaque to clients (the `seq` of the
last returned entry).

CompositorClass.description:
The SA-0 composite-usability classification of the resolved wgpu adapter
(ADR-0035): the acceleration tier the compositor actually runs on. `None`
means no adapter resolved — the CPU composite path only.

CompositorDeviceType.description: The kind of graphics device backing the compositor adapter.

ConfigRevision.description: One immutable revision of a target's config/layout document.

author.description: The principal that committed this revision (its key id / subject).

message.description: A short human commit message (e.g. `"expand to 9 cells"`).

target.description: The stable target key this revision belongs to (e.g. `layout:wall`).

ConnectionRequest.description: An IS-05 connection request `PATCH`ed to a `/staged` endpoint.

master_enable.description: Whether the sender/receiver is enabled once active.

sender_id.description: For a receiver: the sender id to subscribe to (the connection target).

transport_file.description: For a receiver: the SDP transport file describing the sender's stream.

transport_params.description: One transport-param block per leg (1 for single-path, 2 for ST 2022-7).

ConnectionState.description:
The IS-05 connection state of one endpoint: its current active params and any
pending staged change.

active.description: The currently-active transport params (empty until first activated).

oneOf.description: A staged-but-not-yet-active change, if one is pending.

staged_at.description:
The TAI instant (`<seconds>:<nanoseconds>`) the pending change was staged
at, captured so an `ActivateScheduledRelative` offset has a base to
resolve against. [`None`] when nothing is staged, or when the stage was
recorded without a clock stamp.

ConsentActor.description:
Who recorded a telemetry-consent change.

The local machine UI/API or the (later, O1-gated) portal mirror. Serialised
lower-case so the slug is stable across the machine and the portal.
`#[non_exhaustive]` so a future actor is additive on the wire.

ConsentResource.description:
The `GET /api/v1/telemetry/consent` body: the recorded consent document
(ADR-0052 §2). `enabled` is the outbound-daily-pipe consent (off by default);
`changed_at` is the RFC 3339 instant it was last written (absent when never
written); `actor` is who wrote it (`local` | `portal`).

actor.description: Who wrote the record: `local` (the machine UI/API) or `portal`.

changed_at.description:
When the record was last written (RFC 3339); `None` when never written
(the opt-in default).

enabled.description: Whether the outbound daily telemetry pipe is consented (default `false`).

ConsentSetRequest.description: The `PUT /api/v1/telemetry/consent` request body: the new consent state.

enabled.description: Whether to consent to the outbound daily telemetry pipe.

name.description:
One of the environment-variable NAMES the configuration references
(`[network.tls]` EAB names, `[network.tls.dns]` credential names).

value.description: The secret value. Write-only: never logged, never echoed.

item.description: The item to put on preview.

DataRequest.description:
One inbound data request awaiting **local approval**: support (or the licence
server, over the later transport) asks for additional data; nothing leaves
until the operator approves it here (ADR-0053 §3).

detail.description:
An optional structured detail (e.g. the ticket the request relates to).
Never the requested data.

request_id.description: The request id (the `DR-xxxx` / portal correlation key when synced).

requested_at_nanos.description: The media-timeline timestamp (nanoseconds) the request was recorded.

what.description:
A human-readable description of what is being requested (never the data
itself — this is the *ask*, not the payload).

DataRequestActioned.description:
The `200` body of a data-request approve/deny: the request's new terminal
state.

DataRequestState.description:
The lifecycle state of an inbound data request. Approve/deny are one-way; an
elapsed (un-actioned) request is `Expired` (`410 request_expired`).

id.description: Data source id.

DataSourceView.description: A data source with its live status.

used_by.description: Item ids bound to this source.

DetectionZoneDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::DetectionZone` (normalized
sub-rectangle of a tile, `0.0..=1.0` on both axes).

node_id.description: The id of the node hosting this device.

receivers.description: The receiver ids this device exposes.

senders.description: The sender ids this device exposes.

Device.description: An IS-04 **Device**: a logical grouping of senders/receivers on a node.

DeviceAuthDoc.description: `OpenAPI` mirror of the `[devices.auth]` block: a write-only secret reference.

DeviceBodyDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_config::Device`] (ADR-M008): the config-as-code
managed-device document.

Serde-equivalent to the config type field-for-field; the runtime status is a
separate read-only projection ([`DeviceStatusDoc`]), never carried here.

address.description:
Management address, IPv6-first (e.g. `http://[fd00:db8::42]`). Required
for `zowietek`/`cast`; optional for `displaynode`.

alarm_on_offline.description:
The lowercase X.733 severity raised when the device stays offline
(`warning`/`minor`/`major`/`critical`); absent disables the alarm.

oneOf.description: Write-only credentials (the export emits the ref string only).

desired_mode.description: The desired converged work mode (driver vocabulary, e.g. `decoder`).

driver.description: The compiled-in driver family managing this device.

id.description: Stable device id; may be omitted (the path id is injected).

oneOf.description: Supervised-reconnect backoff bounds; absent uses the driver defaults.

spare_decode_index.description:
The explicit spare decode index targeted by an index-scoped `zowietek`
decoder convergence (issue #55). Absent ⇒ the driver never guesses an
index and refuses rather than disrupt an unknown decode.

DeviceDriverDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_config::DeviceDriver`] (ADR-M008): the
compiled-in device-driver families, `snake_case` on the wire.

stable_id.description: The vendor's stable device handle (UUID / PCI bus id / registryID).

DeviceStatusDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_events::DeviceStatus`] (ADR-M008 §2.1): the
read-only latest-wins runtime status `GET /devices/{id}/status` returns.

Serde-equivalent to the event type; runtime telemetry only — never persisted
or exported (config-as-code carries the durable desired state).

device_id.description: The registry device id this snapshot describes.

last_seen_ts.description: Engine monotonic nanoseconds the device last answered, once it has.

mode.description: The device's current converged mode (driver vocabulary), once known.

state.description:
The device's lifecycle state, uppercase on the wire (e.g. `ADOPTING`,
`ONLINE`, `DEGRADED`, `AUTH_FAILED`, `UNREACHABLE`).

temperature_c.description: Device-reported temperature (°C), where the vendor exposes it.

Diagnostics.description: The utilisation/diagnostics summary a bundle carries over its window.

cpu_p0.description: CPU busy-fraction floor (p0) over the window.

cpu_p100.description: CPU busy-fraction ceiling (p100) over the window.

cpu_p50.description: CPU busy-fraction median (p50) over the window.

cpu_p95.description: CPU busy-fraction 95th percentile over the window.

reconnects.description: The number of per-input reconnects recorded in the window.

samples.description: Total utilisation samples folded across the window.

shed_events.description: The number of shed-load events recorded in the window.

DiagnosticsSnapshot.description:
The assembled diagnostics snapshot bundle (`GET /api/v1/diagnostics/{id}`).

The `diagnostics` section is the **shared** [`crate::support_bundle::Bundle`]
the #111 context-pack composer produces — utilisation percentiles + shed/
reconnect counts, incident markers, and the redacted config — so this snapshot
and the support-ticket context-pack draw their diagnostics from one source of
truth (the consent-independent retention store + the config redactor). Logs +
engine state, **never** media, raw identifiers, or secrets (brief §8).

assembled_at_unix_seconds.description: The Unix second the snapshot was assembled.

diagnostics.description:
The redacted diagnostics bundle (the shared #111 composer output): logs +
engine state, never media.

DiscoveredEndpoint.description:
One resolved management endpoint of a discovered service: a presentation-
ready address and its family. IPv6 is the lead family (ADR-0042); IPv4 is
labelled [`AddressFamily::Ipv4Legacy`]. IPv6 literals are bracketed so the
`host:port` form is URL-safe.

family.description:
The address family — `ipv6` (lead) or `ipv4-legacy`. The shared
[`AddressFamily`] enum carries no `ToSchema`, so the schema models the
wire string directly (the same `ipv6` / `ipv4-legacy` tokens serde emits).

DiscoveredService.description:
One **untrusted** discovery-inventory row: a classified, AAAA-first service
requiring explicit confirm-adopt (ADR-0041). It carries **no registry id** —
it is not a device.

domain.description:
The discovery **domain** the observing node stamped on this row
(ADR-W026) — sourced solely from the node's operator-declared
`[discovery] domain` config, **never** from the responder payload, TXT
records, or mesh peer identity. `None` = the observing node declared no
domain; a discovery-scoped principal is denied an unlabelled row
(fail-closed). Event (`device.discovered`) and this REST row are stamped
from the one config value so they can never disagree.

endpoints.description: The management endpoints, **AAAA-first** (IPv6 lead, IPv4 legacy).

key.description:
The dedup key (driver kind + instance name + service type). Two sightings
of the same service share a key and the newer replaces the older.

last_seen_unix_ns.description: When this row was last seen (Unix nanoseconds), informational for the UI.

primary_address.description:
The primary management address — the first (IPv6, if any) endpoint's
`host:port`. This is the address an operator references when confirming
adoption via `POST /devices/{id}`.

txt.description: The decoded TXT records (advertised metadata), key-sorted.

DiscoveryDriverKind.description:
The inferred driver family of a discovered service, from its service type
(and the operator-configured zowietek-control type, if any).

A **closed** `#[non_exhaustive]` enum: a new discoverable family is a new
variant plus a wired browse type, never an open registry. `Unknown` is the
honest catch-all — a service we browsed but cannot classify is reported as
such, never guessed into a family.

DiscoveryModeDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_mesh::DiscoveryMode`] (Conspect, ADR-0051 §2).

Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered `snake_case`. There is exactly **one**
value — `always_on` — and no way to set any other: discovery runs whenever the
account plane runs (the spec's *locked* row, no off switch exists).

DocumentDiff.description:
The added / removed / changed top-level keys between two documents.

A pragmatic, UI-facing structural diff over JSON objects: it reports which
top-level keys were added, removed, or whose value changed. Non-object
documents (or a type change at the root) are reported as a single synthetic
`<root>` change so the diff is always total.

added.description: Keys present in the new document but not the old (sorted).

changed.description: Keys present in both whose value differs (sorted).

removed.description: Keys present in the old document but not the new (sorted).

down_ms.description: Milliseconds the condition must clear before the alarm **clears**.

up_ms.description: Milliseconds the condition must persist before the alarm **raises**.

EffectiveLicense.description:
The effective **build-profile** licence — the codec-linking licence of the
compiled artifact (ADR-0012 / AGENTS.md §G). Distinct from the project's
source-available licence and from NDI's redistribution restriction (carried
separately by [`BuildInfo::ndi`] / [`NdiAttribution`]).

EnforcementLevelDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_licence::EnforcementLevel`].

Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered `kebab-case`. Every level keeps a
running program **on air** (ADR-0050 §6.3, invariant #1) — enforcement is
data the surface renders, never a control-flow decision.

EpgSourceDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::EpgSource` (epg-playlist):
a source's optional per-source EPG (XMLTV) acquisition block.

allow_private_network.description: Whether the feed may resolve to a private/link-local network address.

channel_id.description: Optional exact provider channel id (as it appears in the XMLTV feed).

mode.description: How the guide is obtained. Defaults to `automatic`.

secret_ref.description: Optional secret-manager reference for the feed's credentials.

armed.description: Whether the rule acts (default `false`). Use the arm/disarm routes.

on_break_start.description: What to take at break start.

restore_on_end.description: Restore the pre-break routing at the confirmed end (default `true`).

webhook_url.description: Optional `http://` hook that receives a `POST` on break start/end.

error.description: The last error, if the last attempt failed.

last_attempt.description: Unix seconds of the last attempt.

last_success.description: Unix seconds of the last successful fetch (or 304).

next_attempt.description: Unix seconds of the next scheduled attempt.

url.description: The feed URL with credentials and query removed.

FiredBody.description: The `202` body of a successful salvo fire.

action_id.description: The queued action id (also the pending-action + audit correlation id).

queued_at_nanos.description:
The media-timeline timestamp (nanoseconds, from the ack-clock) the fire
was queued — the audit entry and the pending action share this instant.

FirstLine.description:
The first-line support route a tier maps to (spec §11): a real support queue
for eligible tiers, or the community channel for the free tier.

FocusLimits.description:
Focus caps and occupancy, surfaced by `GET /api/v1/preview/capabilities` so the
UI can tell the truth about how many live viewers the server admits.

max_per_scope.description: Maximum concurrent focus sessions per scope.

attempted_at.description: Last attempt, good or bad (RFC 3339 UTC).

oneOf.description: No GPU cap — the `over_gpu` reason can never fire.
At most this many GPUs may be in use before the `over_gpu` reason fires.

value.description: At most this many GPUs may be in use before the `over_gpu` reason fires.

GpuLimitDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_licence::GpuLimit`].

Serde-equivalent: adjacently tagged on `kind`, value under `value`,
`snake_case` tags (`{"kind":"unlimited"}` / `{"kind":"limited","value":2}`).

HardwareClassDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_licence::HardwareClass`].

Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered `snake_case`.

detected.description: The class detected on the machine (a mismatch is a ladder reason).

licensed.description: The class the entitlement is licensed for.

HealthWarningDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_events::HealthWarning`] (SA-0).

The body of `GET /api/v1/health`: an actionable health warning carrying a
stable `code` + a `remediation`. A round-trip test (`tests/health.rs`) pins
this shape to the real `multiview_events::HealthWarning` so they cannot drift.

active.description: Whether the condition is currently active.

code.description: The stable catalog code — the dedupe key the store + UI coalesce on.

message.description: A clear, human-readable description of the condition.

remediation.description: The concrete remediation — what the operator must do to fix it.

since.description: When the condition was first raised (engine monotonic nanoseconds).

HeartbeatStatus.description:
The read-only heartbeat-status surface (`GET /api/v1/licensing/heartbeat-status`).

This reports **honestly from local lease state** — the transport the active
lease arrived over, the lease install instant as `last_at`, the lease's
`next_contact_due` as `next_due`, and the exhaustive payload-field list —
regardless of whether the cli's feature-gated `heartbeat` loop
(CONSPECT-3/ADR-0096) is the producer that installed the lease (it drives the
same `LeaseStore::install_binding` convergence the offline file-drop uses).
There is **no** mutating endpoint for the heartbeat (the spec mandates none) —
the `POST /api/v1/account/licence/heartbeat` force-now action is a later,
feature-gated item (brief §11 #4), not this read surface.

last_at.description:
The instant this machine last accepted a lease (the install instant), RFC
3339; `None` when no lease is installed (no heartbeat yet — honest).

next_due.description:
When the next licensing contact is due (the active lease's
`next_contact_due`), RFC 3339; `None` when no lease is installed.

payload_fields.description:
The exhaustive list of fields a heartbeat payload carries
([`HEARTBEAT_PAYLOAD_FIELDS`]) — reported, never raw identifiers (§8).

transport.description:
The transport the active lease arrived over: `"direct"` (online server
contact), `"relay"` (mesh relay), or `"file"` (a dropped offline lease).
`"none"` when no lease is installed.

Incident.description: One incident marker in a bundle (a diagnostic event — never media).

at_unix_seconds.description: The Unix second the incident was recorded.

subject.description: What the incident applied to (input id, `program`, `system`, …).

cell.description: The cell id the index resolves to.

index.description: The zero-based source/display index in the tally protocol.

guide_refresh_minutes.description:
Minutes between background guide refreshes while publication is
enabled (default 30, 5..=1440).

public_base_url.description: Optional absolute public base URL for playlist links (default: request Host).

allow_direct_source_url.description: Explicit permission to publish a source's upstream URL (required for sources).

kind.description: Whether `ref` names an output or a source.

ref.description: The referenced output id or source id.

tvg_id.description: Published `tvg-id` override (also the guide channel id).

config.description: The publication document (entries filtered to the caller's scope).

entries.description: Every entry resolved against the current configuration.

feeds.description: Per upstream XMLTV feed refresh status.

guide_generated_at.description: Unix seconds the current guide snapshot was assembled, if any.

guide_path.description: Server path of the published guide.

playlist_path.description: Server path of the published playlist.

Is10Claims.description:
An IS-10 JWT **claims set** (the decoded token body).

Carries the registered claims IS-10 mandates plus the NMOS `x-nmos-api`
claim. Times are Unix seconds (the JWT `NumericDate`).

aud.description:
The audience (the resource server this token is for) — `aud`.

IS-10 allows a single audience or a list; a single value is modelled as a
one-element list on decode by the caller.

id.description: Item id.

JobView.description: Public job status projection with no URL, credentials, document or disk path.

artifact_id.description: Present only after the immutable artifact is committed.

resources.description: Estimated producer resources; GPU remains unknown.

state.description: Queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled or uncertain.

JournalClockSource.description: Which clock produced a wall-clock prediction.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next older page; absent on the last page.

stats.description: Journal counters; `dropped` above zero means the history has gaps.

JournalRecord.description: One raw observation with its full decode.

clock_reference.description: Whether this is a clock stamp rather than an event.

error.description: Why the payload could not be fully decoded.

last_seen_at.description: When the last identical sighting arrived.

raw_encoding.description: `base64` for binary payloads, `text` for HLS tag lines.

received_ns.description: Host receive time, decimal nanoseconds past the Unix epoch.

record_id.description: Sortable identity, assigned by the writer; also the page cursor.

source_pts.description:
90 kHz time of the carrying packet. SCTE-35 sections have no PES header, so
the demuxer reports the last PCR, which trails video PTS by the mux delay.

dropped.description: Observations dropped because the bounded queue was full.

repeats.description: Exact repeats folded into a counter since start.

JournalTiming.description: Times derived for one marker. Predictions, never engine state.

airs_at.description: Predicted instant the splice reaches this multiview's output, UTC.

airs_end_at.description: Predicted instant the break end reaches this multiview's output, UTC.

oneOf.description: Clock used for the wall-clock fields.

end_at.description: Predicted break end on the source, UTC.

pre_roll_ms.description: Splice point minus carrying packet time; negative means already past.

splice_pts.description: Splice point on the source timeline, 90 kHz, after `pts_adjustment`.

start_at.description: Predicted splice wall-clock on the source, UTC.

JournalTimingClass.description: How a marker's time was derived.

media_sequence.description: HLS media sequence of the carrying segment.

segment_uri.description: Carrying segment URI, without query or credentials.

LadderStateDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_licence::LadderState`] (the seven conditions).

Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered `snake_case`.

Layout.description:
A persisted layout resource.

The `body` is the opaque, validated layout document the editor produces; the
control plane stores and version-stamps it without interpreting its
internals here. (Engine-side validation against `multiview-config` happens
before a layout is applied.)

body.description: The opaque layout document (canvas + cells), as canonical JSON.

id.description: Stable resource id.

LayoutInput.description:
The fields a create/update accepts (the id is supplied separately on create
and immutable on update).

LayoutProjectionStatus.description: The projection's health as reported on `GET /api/v1/config/boot-model`.

consecutive_failures.description: Failed attempts since the projection was last healthy.

degraded.description:
Whether the projection differs from the accepted envelope because a
write failed. Layout reads stay correct either way: they use the envelope.

degraded_since_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the first failure of the current fault.

last_error.description:
The most recent failure, while degraded. Withheld from a scoped principal,
because a repository error can name any layout.

repaired_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the last repair that cleared a fault.

retrying.description:
Whether a repair is running or waiting for its next attempt. `degraded`
with `retrying: false` means the retry budget is spent, and the next
commit or restart repairs the projection.

LeaseDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_licence::Lease`] (the dated entitlement
bounds, ADR-0050 §4).

Serde-equivalent: the dated fields are RFC 3339 date-time strings (how
`chrono`'s `DateTime<Utc>` serialises), the day counts are integers.

grace_days.description: The number of grace days that follow expiry.

grace_until.description: The end of the grace window (RFC 3339).

hard_at.description: The absolute hard bound from grant (RFC 3339).

next_contact_due.description: When the next heartbeat is due (RFC 3339).

serial.description: The opaque lease serial (server-issued; not a hardware identifier).

source.description: Where this grant came from (drives the term).

LeaseInstalled.description:
The `200` body of a successful `POST /api/v1/licence/lease` install: the
installed lease's serial and its `valid_to` (the lease term expiry, RFC 3339).

serial.description: The serial of the lease that was verified + installed.

valid_to.description: The instant the installed lease term expires (RFC 3339).

LeaseInstalledDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` body of a successful `POST /api/v1/licence/lease` install: the
installed lease's serial + its `valid_to` (the lease's `expires_at`, RFC
3339). Mirrors the [`crate::routes::licence::LeaseInstalled`] handler shape.

serial.description: The serial of the lease that was verified + installed.

valid_to.description: The instant the installed lease term expires (RFC 3339).

LeaseSourceDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_licence::LeaseSource`].

Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered `snake_case` (`online`/`relay`/`file`).

LicenceResource.description:
The computed licence resource rendered at `GET /api/v1/licence`.

A single shape that always serialises (never `5xx`): `licensed` is `true` with
the full computed `status` when a verified lease is installed, and `false`
with `status: null` when none is — an honest "unlicensed" data report rather
than an error. The control plane, the chrome banner, and the portals all read
the same computed `status.enforcement` level; there is no second opinion.

licensed.description: Whether a verified lease is currently installed.

oneOf.description: The computed licence status when a lease is installed; `None` otherwise.

LicenceStatusDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_licence::LicenceStatusView`] — the computed
licence resource `GET /api/v1/licence` renders.

Serde-equivalent to the real view. The `state`/`enforcement` are **computed**
(the ladder, off the hot loop); every value keeps a running program on air.

blocks_new_instances.description: Whether the startup gate should refuse a new engine instance (S1).

config_locked.description: Whether the engine should deny hot-reconfiguration (derived, S2).

enforcement.description: The canonical enforcement level derived from the state.

gpu_limit.description: The GPU allowance carried by the entitlement.

gpus_in_use.description: The number of GPUs currently in use (informs the `over_gpu` reason only).

lease.description: The dated lease this status reflects.

reasons.description: Machine-readable reason codes the UI renders.

state.description: The computed ladder state (the seven conditions).

tier.description: The opaque commercial tier (rendered, never computed).

watermark.description: Whether the engine should stamp a corner watermark (derived, S3).

LogLevelDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_telemetry::LogLevel`] (ADR-0060): the five
`tracing` severities. Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered lowercase.

LogRecordDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_telemetry::LogRecord`] — one structured
record in the `GET /api/v1/logs` tail (ADR-0060 §2.3).

Serde-equivalent field-for-field to the real record: the optional resource
attribution (`run_id` / `resource_kind` / `resource_id` / `label`), the libav
`component` / `repeated`, and the always-present `seq` / `timestamp_ms` /
`level` / `target` / `message`. Optionals are omitted when absent — an
unattributed line carries no `resource_id` (honesty over a wrong id, §3.3).

component.description: The libav component class (`hevc`, `hls`), for bridge records.

label.description: The resource's human label, if the span carried one.

repeated.description:
The coalesced suppressed-repeat count, when a bridge record flushes a
summary.

resource_id.description: The stable config resource id this record is attributed to, if any.

oneOf.description: The resource kind this record is attributed to, if any.

run_id.description: The process run id, when configured.

seq.description: Monotonic capture sequence number (the cursor for the `since` filter).

timestamp_ms.description: Wall-clock capture time, milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

LogResourceKindDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_telemetry::LogResourceKind`] (ADR-0060 §2.2):
the resource a log record is attributed to. Serde-equivalent: a unit enum
rendered `snake_case`.

skipped.description:
Lines skipped because they were malformed (e.g. a URL without a usable
scheme) — informational.

url_tvg.description:
The header's XMLTV guide URL(s) (`url-tvg` / `x-tvg-url`; a
comma-separated value is split), in declaration order.

name.description: The display name (text after the `#EXTINF` comma), or the URL when absent.

allow_private_network.description:
Permit a catalogue on a private/LAN address (loopback, link-local and
metadata addresses are always refused).

url.description: An http(s) URL of an extended-M3U catalogue to fetch (bounded, SSRF-screened).

MediaFormat.description: The media format of a sender/receiver (the IS-04 `format` URN family).

MeshPeerDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_mesh::Peer`] — a single entry in the untrusted
discovered-peer inventory `GET /api/v1/mesh/peers` returns.

Serde-equivalent to the real peer. The `key` is the salted-digest **hex** id
(64 chars, never a raw identifier — brief §8); `name` is present only once the
operator has confirm-adopted + named the peer; `last_seen` is whole seconds;
`relaying_for_us` is an operator-set adoption flag, never auto (the peer is
**untrusted** until explicitly confirm-adopted — ADR-0041 doctrine).

claimed.description: Whether the peer advertised itself as claimed (observed from the announce).

key.description: The peer's salted-digest id (64-char lowercase hex; never a raw identifier).

last_seen.description: The whole-seconds monotonic instant the peer was last seen.

OutputBodyDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::Output` (tagged by `kind`) — the body
accepted by `POST`/`PUT /api/v1/outputs/{id}`.

`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::OutputFlip` (ADR-0089 §2.2). A flip is
pixel-only (no container "flip" tag), so it forces the pixels path.

OutputLinkDoc.description:
Live link state of a push output (SRT / RTMP / RIST / UDP) — the body of
`GET /api/v1/outputs/{id}/link`.

discarded_awaiting_keyframe.description:
Packets discarded while a fresh session waited for its first video
keyframe. Expected and benign: the link is fine, the decoder is simply
not started yet.

discarded_no_client.description:
Packets discarded because no peer was attached (a listener waiting for a
caller, or a caller between sessions). Expected and benign.

dropped.description:
Packets dropped for this output, for any reason: the sum of the four
reason counters below.

dropped_slow_peer.description:
Packets lost to a slow peer: its bounded-queue overflow, plus every
packet held until it is re-admitted on the next video keyframe (audio
and non-IDR video alike). A real delivery failure.

dropped_upstream.description:
Packets dropped upstream of the distributor (the producer shed a packet
or held its post-loss gate).

last_error.description:
The current link error, if any since the last successful connect. Never
a peer session ending (that is `last_session_error`).

last_session_error.description:
How the most recent peer session ended, when it ended with an error and
no newer peer is attached. Historical context, not current link health.

peers.description: Attached peer addresses: an SRT listener's callers, or a caller's target.

OutputMetadataDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::OutputMetadata` (ADR-0088): per-output
declarative metadata intent, projected onto whatever the transport can carry.

Service/program title (TS SDT `service_name`, RTMP `onMetaData` title,
container `title`, SDP `s=`).

refusals.description: Refusals the take would meet (empty = takeable).

encoder_sessions.description: `"N of M in use"` — whole-system principals only.

fits.description: Whether the take fits the encoder budget now.

new_encoders.description: `0` when an existing encoder carries the feed, `1` for a new one.

urls.description:
This output's viewer playback URL(s) (one or more; a push-only
transport returns a single no-URL entry with an explanatory note).

OutputRouteRequest.description: The body of an output plan / take.

oneOf.description: Optional audio (take only; `follow` is the only slice-1 value).

audio.description: The configured audio feed (`"follow"` unless set).

effective_audio.description:
What the audio carries now: `"program"` (the program mix),
`{"source": id}`, `"preview_source"`, or `{"redacted": true}`.

output.description: The output's API id (the id `/api/v1/outputs/{id}` addresses).

oneOf.description: A take held by the fresh gate (engine readback).

since_tick.description: The tick the current feed went on air (engine readback).

state.description:
`configured` until the engine reports readback for this output, then
`on_air` / `pending` / `degraded` (`redacted` with a hidden feed).

tally.description:
Whether the feed follows the switcher (`program`) or is direct
(`source`) or the preview bus — the tally distinction (§8).

video.description:
The configured video feed: `{"bus": "program"}`, `{"source": "vt1"}`,
or `{"redacted": true}` when the caller may not read the feed.

OutputStream.description: The stream of an output a take re-points.

OutputTakeAccepted.description: The `202` body of an output take.

adopt.description:
When the engine adopts the take: `next_tick`. Only on the request
that enqueued it; a replay never claims a new adoption.

outcome.description: The recorded terminal outcome, on a replay once known.

status.description:
`accepted` (this request enqueued the take), `pending` (a replay of a
reserved key whose outcome is not known yet) or `settled` (a replay
carrying the recorded outcome).

tick.description: The tick of the recorded outcome, on a replay once known.

OutputTakeAudio.description: The audio request of an output take; slice 1 accepts only `follow`.

OutputTally.description: How an output's feed relates to the switcher (ADR-0108 §8 tally).

OutputTarget.description: The output end of an output crosspoint (`kind = "output"`).

output.description: The output API id (the id `/api/v1/outputs/{id}` addresses).

stream.description: The stream re-pointed: only `video` in slice 1.

OutputTargetKind.description: The target of an output crosspoint, tagged on `kind` (never untagged).

OutputTimedMetadataDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::OutputTimedMetadata` (ADR-0088 §4):
the HLS/TS now-playing/cue timed-metadata carrier opt-ins.

id3.description: Emit in-band ID3 metadata frames as MPEG-TS PES.

OutputsUpdatedEntryDoc.description:
One output a routing `PUT`'s rename/removal propagation rewrote
(ADR-R005 §4.3): a renamed or removed discrete `target_track` the output's
`mode = "tracks"` selection carried is rewritten in the SAME atomic commit
as the routing replace — never left dangling, never requiring a
hand-staged intermediate PUT.

removed.description: Track names dropped from this output's selection.

renamed.description: Discrete tracks this output's selection now follows under a new name.

OverlayBodyDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::Overlay` — the body accepted by
`POST`/`PUT /api/v1/overlays/{id}`.

Overlay kinds carry a large, kind-dependent parameter set captured verbatim
(lossless round-trip), so the schema documents the common envelope and
leaves the per-kind extras additive.

id.description: Stable overlay id; may be omitted (the path id is injected).

target.description: Attachment target (`canvas` or a cell id).
The tally target the override applies to.

source.description:
`{"source": id}` or `"none"` (this slice); `{"layout": id}`,
`{"bus": ..}`, `"follow"` arrive in later slices.

PatchDestination.description:
One crosspoint destination: a mixer input (`{"mixer","input"}`) or, in a
later slice, an output slot (`{"output","slot"}`).

output.description: Output id (output slots arrive in a later slice; refused here).

can_take.description: `true` when every crosspoint can be taken.

class.description: Change class (a mixer re-patch is Class-1, hot).

PatchRequest.description: Plan/take body: 1..=64 crosspoints applied atomically at one tick.

on_air.description: On-air guard for the input on Program.

action_id.description: The opaque, unique action id (a UUID) the cancel/execute paths address.

detail.description:
An optional structured detail (e.g. the salvo name a `salvo` action
fires). Never contains secrets.

requested_at_nanos.description: The media-timeline timestamp (nanoseconds) the action was queued.

requested_by.description: The principal (or portal/system actor) that requested the action.

PendingActionKind.description:
The kind of remote action queued for local approval/execution.

Serialised `kebab-case` so the slug is stable across the machine and the
portal. `#[non_exhaustive]` so a future action kind adds a variant without
breaking the wire contract.

PendingActionState.description:
The lifecycle state of a queued action.

An action is `Pending` until it is either `Executed` (it ran) or `Cancelled`
(the operator cancelled it locally first). Both terminal states are immutable
once reached — the local cancel cannot be undone by a later execution, and an
executed action cannot be retroactively cancelled (local-always-wins applies
only *before* execution).

PendingRoute.description: A take in progress on one output.

held_ticks.description: Ticks the take has been held.

PerceivedSeverityDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_core::alarm::PerceivedSeverity`] (X.733).

oneOf.description: `null` when the crosspoint can be taken.

PlaybackUrlDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_config::playback::PlaybackUrl`] — one
viewer playback URL (or no-URL note) for an output
(`GET /api/v1/outputs/{id}/playback`, ADR-0101).

label.description: Short human label, e.g. `"SRT (caller)"` or `"HLS playlist"`.

notes.description:
Extra operator-facing notes: an encryption-passphrase reminder, a
redacted push destination, a missing-host explanation. Never a secret.

The URL a viewer pastes into VLC/ffplay/a browser. Absent when this
output has no viewer-reachable address — see `notes` for why.

The exact shell command an operator pastes to open this URL in VLC
(`None` when [`url`](Self::url) is `None`). For an SRT row this is
VLC's own `vlc --srt-latency=<ms> srt://host:port` form — NOT

`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::PlaylistMetadata` (epg-playlist):

oneOf.description: One-shot transition override (the channel preset otherwise).

The `GET /api/v1/preview/capabilities` response (ADR-P006 move 6): what preview
transports this build can serve, so the SPA picks WHEP vs the JPEG ladder
(ADR-W020) **before** issuing an offer.

The always-available fallback transport literal: `"jpeg"` (the one
fallback literal everywhere — ADR-P006 move 6).

Whether this build can serve WHEP/WebRTC at all (a native transport is
wired). `false` on a pure / negotiation-only build.

An RFC 9457 problem-details document.

path or an operation id).

in the capabilities response so the SPA can label the program preview before
it opens one.

`OpenAPI` mirror of the `[devices.reconnect]` block: supervised-reconnect

What a single redaction removed/masked, surfaced in the preview so the
operator sees exactly what was taken out (never the value itself).

The dotted path of the redacted field (e.g. `cam-1.auth.secret_ref`). A
location, never the value.

Why it was redacted: `secret` (a reference-only secret, removed) or `url`
(a transport URL, masked).

RedactionReason.description: Why a field was redacted from a bundle.

An IS-04 **registration request**: the `{type, data}` body posted to a
Registry's `POST /x-nmos/registration/v1.3/resource`.

The `data` is the resource JSON for the declared `type`. Modelled internally
tagged on `type` (never `untagged`) so it round-trips robustly. The payload

One discrete-track rename a routing `PUT`'s propagation applied to an
output (ADR-R005 §4.3).

original.description: Source the cell showed before the break (restored at the end).

epg_feed.description: The upstream XMLTV feed (redacted) this entry's guide comes from.

The playable URL: an absolute URL for sources, a server path
(`/hls/…`) for outputs. `None` when not playable (see `unavailable`).

A persisted management resource: a stable `id`, a display `name`, and the
opaque `body` document (the config-as-code shape as canonical JSON).

body.description: The opaque resource document, as canonical JSON.

id.description: Stable resource id.

The IS-04 fields common to every resource.

Flattened into each resource type with `#[serde(flatten)]` so the wire JSON
is a flat object (as IS-04 defines), not a nested `core` object.

id.description: The resource UUID (a stable identifier, opaque string here).

tags.description: Free-form tags (each key maps to a list of string values, per IS-04).

The TAI version `<seconds>:<nanoseconds>` ordering updates to this
resource (a newer version supersedes an older one).

The fields a create/update accepts (the id is supplied separately on create
and immutable on update).

Human-friendly name. Optional on the wire: a create/update that omits it
(e.g. a programmatic seed that only carries the typed `body`) defaults to
an empty name rather than failing deserialization — the display name is a
label, never load-bearing, and callers that care always supply one.

operation_id.description: The operation id this revert is correlated under.

`true` when a replayed `Idempotency-Key` answered from the original
reservation (nothing was re-applied; the other fields are this

Whether the revert FULLY applied (`false` ⇒ either Running already
equalled Loaded and nothing was enqueued, or — when
[`shed`](Self::shed) is non-zero — the revert applied only partially).

How many engine commands were shed on a full command bus (review M4):
`0` ⇒ every command landed; non-zero ⇒ the stores were reverted but
the engine may not reflect every change — retry the revert once the
bus drains (the `config-file-apply-incomplete` warning is raised).

Per-section applied/warned summary parts from the one apply machinery
(e.g. `sources: in_a changed`).

RistEncryptionDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::RistEncryption` (PSK; secret by
reference only — never a plaintext key).

secret_ref.description:
Reference to the pre-shared passphrase (`op://…` / `env:VAR`); resolved
at run time, never stored or logged in plaintext.

RistOptionsDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of `multiview_config::RistOptions` (typed RIST connection
options; lowered to the `rist://…?…` `AVIO` URL on the Tier-0 `FFmpeg` path).

bonding.description: Tier-2 only: bonding/load-sharing peers (rejected on the Tier-0 build).

buffer_ms.description:
Recovery/jitter buffer depth in milliseconds (the `ARQ` window;
`0`/absent ⇒ `librist` auto).

Role.description:
A coarse role governing which actions a principal may perform.

Ordered by privilege: `ReadOnly < Viewer < Operator < Admin`. [`Role::can`]
expresses the action gate.

`ReadOnly` and `Viewer` are both read-only at the action gate; they differ in
intent and ordering: `ReadOnly` is the floor (e.g. an audit/compliance role
that should never appear in a write-capable context), while `Viewer` is the
conventional observer. Keeping them distinct lets deployments and the
claims→role mapping express least privilege precisely without changing the
write gate.

to.description: The revision id to restore (a new revision is appended).

RouteClass.description:
The #11 class of a crosspoint take — the three tiers the capability matrix
defines, surfaced **before** the take applies.

Serialised in `snake_case` (`"class1"` / `"reset_lite"` / `"class2"`) and
**never `untagged`**. `#[non_exhaustive]` for forward compatibility.

The classified plan for a crosspoint take: the #11 class plus a
coerced-degradation flag.

Whether the (would-be Class-2) take was **coerced** to Class-1 by an
operator-confirmed down/up-mix to the destination's pinned layout — a

TxtRecord.description: One advertised TXT key/value record (serializable, sortable).

value.description: The TXT value (decoded as UTF-8 by the browser).

cell.description: The cell id whose UMD label changes.

public.description: Explicitly use the public unauthenticated page. Default requests Premium.

WallCadence.description: Exact wall cadence; never a float frame rate.

WallCell.description: One source's rectangle inside the shared wall picture, in coded pixels.

live.description:
Whether this cell currently carries a picture. A cell without one is
black in the wall; its surface shows the source's own still instead.
Excluded from layout identity: it changes without a new generation.

source.description: Source (input) id whose newest frame fills this rectangle.

WallGeometry.description: `GET /api/v1/preview/wall`: the one shared monitor-wall picture's layout.

cells.description: Source rectangles, sorted by source id.

generation.description: Changes whenever the cell assignment changes.

preview_source.description:
The live Preview-bus source, when a switcher is attached. Filled by the
route from the switcher state, never by the engine worker.

WarningCodeDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_events::WarningCode`] (SA-0 catalog).

Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered as its `kebab-case` variant name.

WarningSeverityDoc.description:
`OpenAPI` mirror of [`multiview_events::WarningSeverity`] (SA-0).

Serde-equivalent: a unit enum rendered as its `snake_case` variant name.

WatchStamp.description: One recorded watch event: when it happened and what it was.

at_ms.description: When the load was applied/rejected, as Unix milliseconds (UTC).

detail.description: What happened: an applied-change summary, or the rejection reason.

active.description: Whether a config-file watcher is running for this process.

applied_count.description: How many file changes have been successfully applied since start.

oneOf.description: The most recent successfully applied load, if any.
The most recent rejected (invalid) load, if any.

path.description:
The watched config file path (absent when no watcher was ever
started; kept after a stop so the status names what *was* watched).

restart_pending.description:
Section names changed on disk that only apply on restart (sorted,
deduplicated; latched until restart — ADR-W020).

id.description: Location id (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, 1–64).

name.description: Display name drawn on the graphic.

WeatherLocationInput.description: The `PUT` body: the location without its id (the id is the path).

WeatherLocationView.description: One location with its latest data and freshness.

forecast.description:
Normalized forecast: `{product, aac, area_name, issued_utc,
issued_local, expires_utc, days: [{date, weekday, icon_code, max_c,
min_c, precis, rain_chance, rain_range, start_local}]}` or `null`.

observation.description:
Latest observation: `{station_name, wmo_id, time_local, time_display,
air_temp_c, apparent_temp_c, rel_humidity_pct, wind_dir, wind_kmh,
gust_kmh, pressure_hpa, rain_since_9am_mm}` or `null`.

oneOf.description: Observation product freshness (`null` when not configured).

status.description:
`ok` | `pending` (no data yet) | `error` (last fetch failed, may still
hold last-good data) | `expired` (forecast past its expiry).

WsTicketResponse.description:
The `POST /api/v1/ws/ticket` response: a short-lived, single-use realtime auth
ticket the browser passes as `?ticket=` on the WS/SSE upgrade (ADR-RT011).

ticket.description:
The opaque single-use ticket. Present it once as `?ticket=` within
`expires_in_secs`; it is consumed on the first WS/SSE upgrade.

YoutubeCapability.description:
The `youtube` source kind's resolve capability (ADR-0015): whether this
build can actually resolve a live `YouTube` URL right now.

available.description:
Whether a `yt-dlp` binary was found and successfully probed
(`yt-dlp --version`) at startup. Always `false` when
[`compiled`](Self::compiled) is `false`.

compiled.description:
Whether the `youtube` Cargo feature is compiled into this binary. A
`false` here means the build simply cannot run the resolver at all,
regardless of whether `yt-dlp` is installed.

version.description:
The probed `yt-dlp --version` output — present only when
[`available`](Self::available) is `true`.

bearer_auth.description: Machine bearer token: a hashed API key or a JWT, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
